events.title: Harvard College Receives Its Name
events.description: The young college in Cambridge, Massachusetts, was named in honor of clergyman John Harvard, its first major donor. His gift of money and books helped keep the fledgling school going.
events.significance: Harvard became the oldest institution of higher learning in the United States and grew into one of the most influential universities in the world.

events.title: William Herschel Discovers Uranus
events.description: Using a telescope in Bath, England, the German-born astronomer William Herschel spotted a new object that turned out to be a planet. It was the first planet found since antiquity.
events.significance: The discovery roughly doubled the known size of the solar system and showed that the heavens still held major surprises.

events.title: Tsar Alexander II Is Assassinated
events.description: Russia's Tsar Alexander II was killed by a bomb in St. Petersburg, in a plot carried out by revolutionaries including Ignacy Hryniewiecki. He died shortly after reforming Russia, including freeing the serfs.
events.significance: His death ended an era of reform in Russia. His successor turned to harsher repression, which shaped the country's path toward later upheavals.

events.title: The Battle of Dien Bien Phu Begins
events.description: Viet Minh forces under General Vo Nguyen Giap opened a massive artillery bombardment on the French garrison at Dien Bien Phu in northern Vietnam.
events.significance: The French defeat that followed ended the First Indochina War and French colonial rule in Indochina, and it set the stage for the later conflict in Vietnam.
